newsitem.title: USA: Abu Marzook to give up extradition challenge.
newsitem.headline: Abu Marzook to give up extradition challenge.

text.p: A Hamas political leader accused in Israel of murder and other violent acts is to give up his effort to resist extradition from the United States, the State Department said on Tuesday.
"We understand that Mr (Mousa Mohammed) Abu Marzook intends to withdraw his legal challenge to the order finding him extraditable," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
"Any such legal decision is of course within Mr Abu Marzook's rights. It's entirely his own choice," Burns said.

Israel announced in 1995 that it had formally asked the United States to hand over Abu Marzook, alleging he was responsible as head of the political arm of Hamas -- a Palestinian Islamist movement -- for attacks that killed scores of Israelis.

Abu Marzook was arrested in July 1995 at a New York airport as he flew to the United States, where he had lived for many years. A U.S. district judge ordered his extradition last May, and the ruling was upheld by another judge in October.
Abu Marzook had appealed the rulings and, according to federal prosecutors, a U.S. government response to his appeal had been due Wednesday. No further details were immediately available.
